executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC (Weeks 16-20, 2026) and PAHO (October 2025-May 2026) reveal a complex multi-threat landscape across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) in the Americas represents the highest-priority biosafety concern, with ongoing animal-sector detections reported across multiple PAHO updates spanning November 2025 through March 2026, constituting a BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential. Additional elevated threats include Mpox (BSL-3), Yellow Fever, Dengue, and a resurgent Pertussis wave across the Americas, alongside seasonal influenza transitions in both hemispheres. Measles re-emergence and Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome round out a dense concurrent threat environment requiring coordinated surveillance and response.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) and Mpox as BSL-3 select agents dominate the threat landscape across the Americas, compounded by simultaneous surges in Dengue, Pertussis, Yellow Fever, and Measles demanding urgent multi-pathogen public health response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates spanning November 2025 through March 2026 indicating sustained detection
Ongoing animal-sector spread with zoonotic spillover risk to humans
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential flagged across two separate PAHO update cycles
threats.action: Immediate activation of One Health surveillance protocols; enhance human-animal interface monitoring; ensure stockpile readiness of antivirals and candidate H5N1 vaccines; report all human exposures to WHO under IHR

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating active transmission
BSL-3 select agent requiring enhanced containment protocols
Ongoing circulation consistent with endemic establishment risk in the Americas
threats.action: Strengthen case detection and contact tracing; ensure vaccine (MVA-BN) availability; implement ring vaccination for confirmed clusters; coordinate with ECDC for cross-regional signal sharing

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 13 March 2026 signaling active risk
Potential sylvatic cycle amplification in endemic zones
Risk of spread to unvaccinated urban populations
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk countries; conduct entomological surveillance for Aedes and Haemagogus vectors; enforce vaccination requirements for travelers from endemic areas

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update 18 February 2026 documenting elevated case counts
Historical pattern of record-breaking seasons in Americas since 2024
Co-circulation risk with Chikungunya and Yellow Fever via shared Aedes aegypti vector
threats.action: Intensify vector control and community-based surveillance; prepare hospital surge capacity; monitor serotype shifts for severe dengue risk; coordinate with ECDC CDTR reports for imported case tracking

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two consecutive PAHO alerts (December 2025 and March 2026) indicating sustained resurgence
Multi-country wave affecting infants and vulnerable populations
Potential waning vaccine immunity contributing to outbreak amplification
threats.action: Audit Tdap and DTaP vaccination coverage; prioritize booster campaigns for pregnant women and healthcare workers; enhance laboratory confirmation capacity; review macrolide prophylaxis protocols for close contacts

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 3 February 2026 indicating active transmission
Region had achieved elimination status; re-emergence signals importation and immunity gaps
Concurrent ECDC CDTR monitoring suggests European crossover risk
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments; deploy outbreak response immunization in affected areas; strengthen port-of-entry surveillance; ensure two-dose MMR verification for travelers

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 19 December 2025
Seasonal rodent population dynamics may be driving increased human exposure risk
High case fatality rate (~35%) warrants vigilance even at lower case counts
threats.action: Enhance rodent control and public awareness campaigns in endemic rural areas; ensure ICU capacity and supportive care protocols; reinforce reporting mechanisms given high mortality

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 10 February 2026
Shares Aedes aegypti vector with Dengue creating co-epidemic risk
Potential geographic expansion as vector range shifts
threats.action: Integrate Chikungunya surveillance into existing Dengue vector control programs; train clinicians on differentiation from Dengue; monitor for neurological complications in vulnerable populations

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents have been detected and flagged in active surveillance reports: (1) Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — documented across two PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026) in the Americas Region animal sector, representing sustained zoonotic threat with pandemic potential requiring IHR notification and enhanced biosafety containment; (2) Mpox virus — documented in PAHO epidemiological update (April 2026) with active human transmission in the Americas, requiring BSL-3 laboratory handling and enhanced contact tracing. Both agents are subject to select agent regulations and require immediate escalation to national biosafety authorities.
amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance patterns should be monitored given multi-country resurgence with two consecutive PAHO alerts
Antiviral resistance surveillance for H5N1 (oseltamivir resistance) is critical given sustained zoonotic activity across the Americas
Methanol poisoning alert (October 2025) may reflect illicit alcohol supply chains that could complicate clinical management of infectious disease patients in affected regions
emergingPatterns: Dual-cycle Avian Influenza A(H5N1) surveillance alerts (November 2025 and March 2026) suggest persistent enzootic establishment rather than isolated spillover events in the Americas

Simultaneous co-circulation of multiple Aedes aegypti-borne viruses (Dengue, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever) across the Americas creates compounding syndromic diagnosis challenges and vector control resource strain
Back-to-back PAHO Pertussis alerts within three months indicate a sustained resurgence wave potentially driven by immunity gaps post-COVID disruptions to routine immunization
Measles re-emergence in a historically elimination-certified region signals dangerous regression in vaccination coverage likely driven by pandemic-era immunization disruptions
Mpox continued transmission into Q2 2026 despite prior international response efforts suggests endemic establishment risk in the Americas

Simultaneous seasonal influenza transitions in both hemispheres (Southern Hemisphere season start and Northern Hemisphere season overlap) create a window of heightened global respiratory virus co-circulation risk
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly CDTR reports (Weeks 16-20) reflects sustained European surveillance alert posture consistent with multiple concurrent threat signals
